So are the old woman in the doorway, Felice Hale, Cecily Hale, Wat, Alfric, Bartle the younger, Lambert, the Dunning lads, Maud the younger and the walkers.

pages.label: change_thing(walk__gate_bar_a_bar)
pages.page: You set your shoulder to it and heave. Wood groans and iron shrieks, and the noise of it goes further than you would like. The camp gate is barred from within with a length of ash, and somebody has chalked a number on the bar.

pages.label: go(walk__arch_a,walk__camp_a)
pages.page: The camp gate is barred from within with a length of ash, and somebody has chalked a number on the bar.

pages.label: listen(walk__gate_bar_a)
pages.page: You put an ear to the camp gate’s bar, and hold your breath. There is nothing to hear from it.

pages.label: go(walk__arch_a,walk__camp_a)
pages.page: The camp gate is barred from within with a length of ash, and somebody has chalked a number on the bar. Ambrose, the Mile-Keeper, who walks at the head of the Walk, is here. Maud, a walker who keeps the roll of the road’s dead, is here.

pages.label: go(region__s1_drill_gate,region__s1_drill)
pages.page: A square of beaten earth behind the Ancient Lantern, a rack of blunted blades along one wall and a post hacked pale at the height of a man’s neck. Whoever teaches here will show a technique to anyone who has done enough to be worth the showing, and can pay for it. Randal teaches Reckless Attack, Dirty Trick and Riposte, 20 coin a lesson: an hour’s work, and only to one who has done enough out in the world to have earned it. On the rack by the gate, for sale and not for practice, are a fine battleaxe, a fine greatsword and a fine shortbow. Randal, a master-at-arms, who teaches for 20 coin a lesson, is here.

pages.label: go(region__s1_scriv_door,region__s1_scriv)
pages.page: A narrow shop that smells of ink and sand: a counter, letters waiting under a stone to be called for, a price for each kind of hand chalked on a board. A heavy curtain hangs across the back of the shop. The scrivener keeps a chair in front of it, and keeps sitting in it. The scrivener, who writes letters for those who cannot, is here.

pages.label: go(fellowship__door_a,fellowship__hall_a)
pages.page: A long low room with a table down the middle and benches either side. On the end wall hangs the roll: the garrison in four columns, one to a hall, each column in its keeper’s hand and each hand different. The table has been cleared at one end and a single sheet squared up on it. Three columns of the roll are ticked to the quarter-day in a thin brown ink. The fourth is ticked as far as the last quarter, and after that there is only the white of the wall. Mabel, the head of the fellowship, is here.

pages.label: talk_to(fellowship__head)
pages.page: ‘Come in, come in, whoever you are,’ says Mabel. ‘Everybody else has.’

pages.label: take_leave(fellowship__head)
pages.page: ‘Off you go, then,’ says Mabel, ‘and don’t do anything I’d be ashamed to hear about. Or do, and tell me.’

pages.label: go(circus__tober_lane_a,circus__tober_a)
pages.page: A grazing field outside Newmeet, sloping a little toward the road, with a five-barred gate and a lime tree. The big top stands in the middle of the field, striped red and dirty white, its king-pole flying a pennant that says WAPSHOTT’S in letters gone pink. Guy-ropes run out from it to stakes in every direction, so that walking anywhere is a kind of dance. Before the flap a painted front of boards announces THE GRAND PEREGRINE CIRCUS & HIPPODRAMA, PATRONIZED BY THE NOBILITY, and someone has written under it in chalk, WHICH NOBILITY. The big top’s king-pole stands up through the canvas, and the pennant snaps. Ada Thripp, the circus’s book-keeper, is here. Signor Cornelius Fipps, the circus’s bandmaster, is here. Gideon Lusk, the circus’s boss canvasman, is here. So are Nance Tibbet and Sidney Quirk. The field gate stands open and the grass inside it is already trodden into paths. A smell of horse and oranges and wet canvas, a dog asleep on a coil of rope, and a man somewhere out of sight shouting HEAVE in a voice like a gong. You have walked into a circus.

pages.label: go(circus__wagon_steps_a,circus__wagons_a)
pages.page: The living-wagons stand in a ring with their shafts down and their steps let down, like a village that walked here: green, yellow, a blue one with stars, a black one with the word SIBYL in gold. Chimneys smoke. On the steps of the biggest, which is crimson and has a brass knocker in the shape of a lion, there is a boot-scraper and a sign: THE COLONEL. KNOCK. WAIT. KNOCK AGAIN. The living-wagons stand shafts-down in their ring. Inside the crimson wagon, over the Colonel’s bunk, hang his relics: a framed bill, a length of iron chain, and a picture in a gilt frame with its face to the wall. Colonel Florian Wapshott, the proprietor of Wapshott’s Grand Peregrine Circus, is here. A woman in a silver wrap is here. Lucius Hench, the circus’s wardrobe-master, is here.

pages.label: go(circus__ring_curtain_a,circus__yard_a)
pages.page: Behind the big top is the backyard, where the circus lives: horse lines, a cookhouse fire with a kettle on a chain, washing on the guy-ropes, a heap of hay, a man asleep in a barrow. Through the gap in the canvas you can hear the ring. Honoria Bulstrode’s cookhouse fire burns under a black kettle and a pot the size of a font. Honoria Bulstrode is frying bacon by the hundredweight in a pan like a cartwheel, and the whole circus is queuing for it in its nightshirts, in order of precedence: the Colonel first, then Bucephalus, then everyone else. Mumchance, the circus’s old clown, is here. Honoria Bulstrode, the Ox of Abernant, strongwoman and cook, is here. Billie Ostrander, the circus’s horse-keeper, is here.

pages.label: go(circus__back_a,circus__tober_a)
pages.page: A grazing field outside Newmeet, sloping a little toward the road, with a five-barred gate and a lime tree. The big top stands in the middle of the field, striped red and dirty white, its king-pole flying a pennant that says WAPSHOTT’S in letters gone pink. Guy-ropes run out from it to stakes in every direction, so that walking anywhere is a kind of dance. Before the flap a painted front of boards announces THE GRAND PEREGRINE CIRCUS & HIPPODRAMA, PATRONIZED BY THE NOBILITY, and someone has written under it in chalk, WHICH NOBILITY. The big top’s king-pole stands up through the canvas, and the pennant snaps. Ada Thripp, the circus’s book-keeper, is here. Signor Cornelius Fipps, the circus’s bandmaster, is here. Gideon Lusk, the circus’s boss canvasman, is here. So are Nance Tibbet and Sidney Quirk.

pages.label: go(region__s5_drill_gate,region__s5_drill)
pages.page: A square of beaten earth behind the Stone Sword, a rack of blunted blades along one wall and a post hacked pale at the height of a man’s neck. Whoever teaches here will show a technique to anyone who has done enough to be worth the showing, and can pay for it. Agnes teaches Whirlwind Attack, Shield Bash and Roundhouse Kick, 35 coin a lesson: an hour’s work, and only to one who has done enough out in the world to have earned it. On the rack by the gate, for sale and not for practice, are a fine battleaxe, a fine scimitar and a fine longbow. Agnes, a master-at-arms, who teaches for 35 coin a lesson, is here.

pages.label: talk_to(region__s5_drill_master)
pages.page: Agnes looks twice, and then a third time. ‘Well. Look who it is.’

pages.label: go(region__s5_drill_gate,region__s5_green)
pages.page: The gate-yard of Sedgeminster is swept clean to the cobbles, and smells of wet stone and beeswax from the chapel door. Letice is sitting on a log by the door, mending a strap and watching the treeline. The brothers’ dog sleeps against the wall of the guest-hall with one ear up for the door. A grey cat sits on a wall-top with her eyes half shut and her tail hanging down the stones. A goat with a broken tether is cropping the verge, with her whole attention. Your brother is sitting on a rail with your father’s old spear across his knees, watching the road. He is taller by a head than when you went away. A grey dog lies by the door of the guest-hall of Sedgeminster with her head on her paws, watching the road. She holds one forefoot off the ground. A notice is nailed to the post by the well, written over in several hands. Perrin, a salter, selling from the house door, is here. The prior, who keeps the rule of the brothers of Reodweard, is here. Aldous Fenn, the reeve of the wood-wardens, who license the cutting in the woods round Sedgeminster, is here. So are the surveyor’s son and Jankin Reeve.

pages.label: go(region__edge_south_road,region__edge_south)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. For a while the road keeps company with a river, close enough to hear it. The last mile is slow going. A march-stone as tall as a man stands by the road where it leaves Faennmeós. On this side it is cut with the sign of Faennmeós; on the far side, with a sign you do not know. Beyond it the road goes on south into Glōmfaenn, fen country, the folk say. Few of them have been.

pages.label: go(region__tl_edge_south,region__t276)
pages.page: A causey of old turves across the marsh, and on either side of it water that does not show how deep it is. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw275_276,region__t275)
pages.page: Water stands on both sides, and the path between is soft enough to take the print of your boot and keep it. Open water and mud among willow stumps, smelling of rot and mint. To the west the land rises. A shepherd with a crook and a young dog at heel, looking about as if for something lost, is here. A whistle, and a young dog comes bounding at you through the grass and stops short, and behind it a shepherd, crook in hand, who calls it off and looks you over.

pages.label: go(region__tw274_275,region__t274)
pages.page: The path goes out across the fen on a raised bank, reed on either hand taller than a man, open water glinting through it. Peat ground cut once into steps, and long since flooded.

pages.label: go(region__tw255_274,region__t255)
pages.page: Out on the fen the sky is enormous, and the only things standing up in all that flatness are you and a heron. Reed-beds whispering in the wind, and a bittern in them booming like a blown jar. To the north-west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw235_255,region__t235)
pages.page: The path runs along a river for a mile, with alders on the bank and the water loud over the stones. Reed-beds whispering in the wind, and a bittern in them booming like a blown jar. The Swanwater runs through it, and has to be waded or gone round. To the north the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw235_256,region__t256)
pages.page: Open water and mud among willow stumps, smelling of rot and mint. To the east the land rises. Tracks cross the ground here, heavy and fresh and all going the one way, north-west, and the same tracks older under them: something uses this way often.

pages.label: go(region__tw257_258,region__t258)
pages.page: The light goes before you are halfway, and you walk the rest by guess and by the pale line of the path. Mist lying on the marsh, the reeds standing up out of it and the ground not showing at all. To the north-west the land rises. A snake, an adder, grey-brown with a dark zigzag down its back, coiled with its head raised, is here.

pages.label: go(region__tw237_258,region__t237)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. Open water and mud among willow stumps, smelling of rot and mint. An otter, a sleek brown otter with a pale throat and a thick tapering tail, rising from the river, is here.

pages.label: go(region__tw218_237,region__t218)
pages.page: Reed-beds whispering in the wind, and a bittern in them booming like a blown jar. To the south-west the land rises. A shepherd with a crook and a young dog at heel, looking about as if for something lost, is here.

pages.label: go(region__tw218_238,region__t238)
pages.page: Alder carr standing in its own black water, the roots like knuckles. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw239_259,region__t259)
pages.page: Peat ground cut once into steps, and long since flooded. A shepherd with a crook and a young dog at heel, looking about as if for something lost, is here. A whistle, and a young dog comes bounding at you through the grass and stops short, and behind it a shepherd, crook in hand, who calls it off and looks you over.

pages.label: go(region__tw277_278,region__t278)
pages.page: Wet ground, sedge and cotton-grass, the pools reflecting the sky, a heron getting up slow and offended.

pages.label: go(region__tw277_278,region__t277)
pages.page: Peat ground cut once into steps, and long since flooded. A snake, an adder, grey-brown with a dark zigzag down its back, coiled with its head raised, is here.

pages.label: go(region__s1_apothecary_door,region__s1_apothecary)
pages.page: Drawers climb to the ceiling, each with a word on it in faded ink, and a ladder on a rail runs along them. The air is dry and bitter, and a cat sleeps on the counter beside the brass scales. Leofric, an apothecary, is here.

pages.label: go(region__s1_apothecary_door,region__s1_green)
pages.page: Boats lie drawn up keel to keel on the shingle at Misthythe, and the houses come right down to them, nets hung on every fence. It is bitterly cold; smoke hangs low over the roofs, and nobody stands about. Woodsmoke hangs low over the roofs, and the fields are bare. Magot is crying wares along the street: pots mended, knives ground. Hild is darning the hem of a red stage cloak. Isot the bookkeeper is weighing a handful of nails on a small brass scale. Averil the conspirator is shuffling a worn pack of cards one-handed. The inn’s dog lies across the doorstep of the Laughing Flame with his chin on his paws, and watches who comes. A thin brown cat crouches at the foot of a wall, watching a hole in it without a blink. A notice is nailed to the post by the well, written over in several hands. A strip of vellum is nailed to the post by the well, in a fair clerk’s hand, with a lead seal pressed in a blob of wax. A tall wagon, painted with a sun and a moon and the words GOSSE’S COMPANY in red letters gone pink, stands on the landing at Misthythe with its shafts down. A chain runs from its back wheel to a post, and the chain has a padlock on it. Wapshott’s bill on the wall says NOW PLAYING, NIGHTLY AT SEVEN, ADMISSION ONE COIN, CHILDREN AND DOGS HALF, on a strip pasted over the word COMING. The spring-head by the green has been running low for a year. The rope comes up with a hand’s depth of brown water in the bucket and a smell of wet stone, and the women who draw it do so in silence, to save breath. Aldous Fenn, the reeve of the wood-wardens, who license the cutting in the woods round Misthythe, is here. Hesper Lowe, a boat-wright’s apprentice with a drawing of a bell, is here. The old woman in the doorway, the innkeeper’s mother, who has not been out of her chair since the harvest and who asks, every morning, whether the lamp has been lit, is here. So are Absalom Gosse, Hepzibah Dimmock and Jem Pudding.

pages.label: go(region__w14_track,region__w14)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. A walled keep stands on a rise above the fields, smoke at its chimneys and a banner over its gate. Reeds hiss in the wind. A lizard watches from a tussock, its throat pulsing. Below the north wall the ditch has been scythed clean in one place, and a stone outfall there breathes out a thread of cold air that smells of old water. Nothing else on the wall has been tended. A banner hangs over the gate, a tower with a star over it in white on green, and under it, lower, a black cloth the width of a hand that has been there some days. Wenna gains 10 experience: found Marsh Garth.

pages.label: search(region__w14)
pages.page: You search a walled keep on its rise with care, a little at a time. Pulling the weed back from the outfall, you find the arch behind it is no drain-mouth but a culvert cut for a man to crawl, and the air coming out of it is cold. The air in the culvert is thick and sweetish. A flame held up in it burns blue and leans back toward the outfall.

pages.label: go(region__tw101_102,region__t101)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. An axe is going in the wood, a long way off, and you never see the woodman. Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed.

pages.label: go(region__tw82_101,region__t82)
pages.page: Larks go up out of the grass on either hand, and come down again behind you. Open country: rough pasture and old field-strips gone back to grass, a hedge here and there, the sky very big over it. To the south the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw61_82,region__t61)
pages.page: The path goes into the wood, and the wood closes over it, and for a long time there is nothing to see but the next bend. Close wood, old and mossy, the paths between the trunks made by animals and going where animals go. Trampled into the bracken by the rooting lies a pack, its strap broken, as if dropped by someone running. The ground under the oaks is rooted up in raw swathes, the earth in them still dark and wet. Whatever did it is not far off. A boar, an old boar with one tusk broken, rooting for mast, is here. A boar comes out of the holly with its head low, and stands, and blows. It does not mean to go round you. A boar is watching you. In 7 minutes it will be on you.

pages.label: go(region__tw42_61,region__t42)
pages.page: For an hour the path runs under trees, and the light comes down green and broken through the leaves. Old coppice gone wild, each stool grown into a clump of stems as thick as a leg. Misthythe is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__tl_z4_edge,region__z4_edge)
pages.page: Here Asholt begins: hazel and thorn at first, then oak, and the light under them goes green. Misthythe is behind you, out in the open. Willows lean out over the water here, grey-green, their roots in the bank and their long shoots trailing in the current. Meadowsweet grows thick along the wet ground, a froth of cream flowers that smells of almonds and honey. Comfrey grows rank by the water, hairy-leaved, its bells hanging: knitbone, the herb-wives call it. A bramble of goodberries grows along the edge of the trees, the berries small and red. Foxgloves stand tall at the wood’s edge, purple bells speckled inside: they heal, prepared rightly, and kill otherwise. Feverwort grows here in the rough grass, bitter-leaved: the herb-wives dry it for a child’s fever. Bamboo grows here in a dense clump, its canes knocking together in the wind. A bay tree grows here, dark and glossy, clipped for its leaves. Celandine grows here, yellow-starred in the damp. Woodbine climbs here, its cream and yellow flowers sweet at dusk. Staggerweed grows here, tall, with spurred blue flowers. A cinnamon tree grows here, its bark peeled in strips. Actaea grows here, its white flowers in feathery spikes. Betony stands in the short grass at the wood’s edge, purple-spiked: the hedge herb, for a cut or a sting.

pages.label: go(region__z4_trail1,region__z4_heart)
pages.page: You set out from the edge of Asholt by Misthythe. It is a long walk, and your feet are sore by the end. A long bank and ditch run through the wood, grown over with trees as old as any around them. It was dug long before anyone now living. Off to one side the undergrowth is broken in a line at the height of a man’s shoulder, not a deer’s: someone goes off this way now and then. A badger’s path runs along the top of the bank. A ditch full of leaves runs along the foot of the bank. Banewort grows here, dark-leaved, with dull purple bells. Alhuren grows here, silver-leaved, its blue flowers pale as a candle-flame. Rosenoble grows here, a briar of deep red roses.

pages.label: go(region__tw100_120,region__t120)
pages.page: Out on the fen the sky is enormous, and the only things standing up in all that flatness are you and a heron. Open water and mud among willow stumps, smelling of rot and mint. To the east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw120_121,region__t121)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. Pine wood, the ground soft with needles and the smell of resin heavy in the still air. To the east the land rises. A hedgehog, a small brown hedgehog with a coat of pale-tipped spines and a pointed, whiskered snout, is here.

pages.label: go(region__tw121_141,region__t141)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. The path goes out across the fen on a raised bank, reed on either hand taller than a man, open water glinting through it. Alder carr standing in its own black water, the roots like knuckles. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw141_142,region__t142)
pages.page: Water stands on both sides, and the path between is soft enough to take the print of your boot and keep it. Wet ground, sedge and cotton-grass, the pools reflecting the sky, a heron getting up slow and offended. To the north the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw142_163,region__t163)
pages.page: The path runs along a river for a mile, with alders on the bank and the water loud over the stones. Fen: reeds taller than a man, black water between, and the ground giving underfoot with every step. The Swanwater runs through it, and has to be waded or gone round. To the north-west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw163_182,region__t182)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. For a while the path keeps company with a river, close enough to hear it. Reed-beds whispering in the wind, and a bittern in them booming like a blown jar. The Swanwater runs through it, and has to be waded or gone round. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw181_182,region__t181)
pages.page: A causey of old turves across the marsh, and on either side of it water that does not show how deep it is. The Swanwater runs through it, and has to be waded or gone round. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__s1_chandlery_door,region__s1_chandlery)
pages.page: Shelves to the ceiling: coils of rope, lamps and lamp-oil, candles in bundles, sacks of meal; everything a traveller forgets, and the smell of tallow over it all. Hankin, a chandler, is here.

pages.label: search(region__s1_chandlery)
pages.page: You search Hankin’s chandlery with care, a little at a time. Nothing is put away or hidden here. You have been over the whole of it, and nothing is hidden here.

pages.label: go(region__gate_lull_road,region__gate_lull)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. The road runs along a river for a mile, with alders on the bank and the water loud over the stones. By the end of it you are footsore and tired. The road goes on into the Lull. Ahead, a bare green hill with a standing stone on it, and a road that goes round the hill and comes back.

pages.label: go(region__tw55_56,region__t55)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. For an hour the path runs under trees, and the light comes down green and broken through the leaves. Birch and rowan on a slope, the light coming white through the leaves. To the north-west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw35_55,region__t35)
pages.page: The path climbs onto open moor, and the country falls away behind you in long brown folds. High ground, rock breaking through the turf, and below, when you turn, the whole country laid out small. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: wait
pages.page: Time passes. A whistle, and a young dog comes bounding at you through the grass and stops short, and behind it a shepherd, crook in hand, who calls it off and looks you over.

pages.label: go(region__tw34_35,region__t34)
pages.page: You set out from the fells of Cloudfell. Sheep stand on the path and move off only when you are close. High ground, rock breaking through the turf, and below, when you turn, the whole country laid out small.

pages.label: go(region__tw16_36,region__t36)
pages.page: The path goes into the wood, and the wood closes over it, and for a long time there is nothing to see but the next bend. Old coppice gone wild, each stool grown into a clump of stems as thick as a leg. To the north the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw36_57,region__t57)
pages.page: Pine wood, the ground soft with needles and the smell of resin heavy in the still air. To the north-west the land rises. Broadford is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__tl_z2_side3,region__z2_side3)
pages.page: Here Ashurst begins: hazel and thorn at first, then oak, and the light under them goes green. Broadford is behind you, out in the open. Yarrow grows in the grass at the wayside, flat white heads over feathery leaves: a soldier’s herb, for cuts. A bramble of goodberries grows along the edge of the trees, the berries small and red. Feverwort grows here in the rough grass, bitter-leaved: the herb-wives dry it for a child’s fever. Bamboo grows here in a dense clump, its canes knocking together in the wind. Banewort grows here, dark-leaved, with dull purple bells. Celandine grows here, yellow-starred in the damp. Cinquefoil runs over the ground here, its small yellow flowers five-petalled. Alhuren grows here, silver-leaved, its blue flowers pale as a candle-flame. Rosenoble grows here, a briar of deep red roses. Woodbine climbs here, its cream and yellow flowers sweet at dusk. A cinnamon tree grows here, its bark peeled in strips. Ofbit grows here on thin stems, its flowers blue. Betony stands in the short grass at the wood’s edge, purple-spiked: the hedge herb, for a cut or a sting.

pages.label: go(region__z2_trail7,region__z2_heart)
pages.page: Ancient pollarded oaks stand about a glade, each one hollow, each with a crown of straight poles cut and grown again for longer than the wood has had its name. Off to one side the undergrowth is broken in a line at the height of a man’s shoulder, not a deer’s: someone goes off this way now and then. An owl sits in one of the hollows, and does not move. Every pollard’s crown is a bundle of straight poles. Bloodroot grows here, broad-leaved, with white flowers low to the ground.

pages.label: go(region__tw11_12,region__t11)
pages.page: Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw18_19,region__t19)
pages.page: Out on the fen the sky is enormous, and the only things standing up in all that flatness are you and a heron. Wet ground, sedge and cotton-grass, the pools reflecting the sky, a heron getting up slow and offended. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tl_edge_east,region__edge_east)
pages.page: The road ends where the land of Faennmeós does, on shingle above the tide-line, and beyond it is the Eastern Ocean, grey and moving as far as can be seen. No road goes on from here; what lies over the water is reached by ship, if at all.

pages.label: go(region__edge_east_road,region__s3_green)
pages.page: You leave the shore of the Eastern Ocean with your hood up and the rain in your face. The smoke of Broadford comes up over the next rise, and then the roofs. At Broadford the houses stand close along the bank where the road goes down into the Broadwater. A rope is strung across the water on posts, green where hands have held it. Beyond the roofs lies the Palewater. The fells rise steeply behind the last houses. The drover’s boy sits on the well-curb with a loaf tied to his wrist, which he is to carry until the spring, and the town files past, one by one, and looks at him, and says nothing, which is the whole of the custom. Nobody has spoken to the drover. The shutters of the sick child’s house stay drawn, and there are flowers on the step. Sir Hamo’s men rode into the market at noon and took a tithe of everything on the stalls, with the reeve standing by because there was nothing he could do. The Broadwater runs knee-deep and clear over the ford stones. A carter stands thigh-deep in the water with his breeches rolled, hauling at the bridle of a horse that will not come. Wellby is roping down a load of barrels. Garret Greenbottle is soldering a hole in a kettle over a little fire, squinting through the smoke. Bree is reading the evening office from a small book, lips moving. Alton Tosscobble is touching up a painted backcloth of a castle with a small brush. The inn’s dog lies across the doorstep of the Golden Bear with her chin on her paws, and watches who comes. A woman in black sits on the step of a cold house with her hands in her lap, watching the road. A drover’s boy of fourteen, seen on the hill the morning after the herd crossed it, is here. Garrow Pelt, an old soldier, who sits by the well and tells a story about a march over the water that nobody asks him to repeat, is here. Fenella Hilltopple, the child’s mother, is here. So are Myrtle Hilltopple and the woman in black. Ghost thumps her tail on the ground without getting up.

pages.label: go(region__s3_chandlery_door,region__s3_chandlery)
pages.page: Shelves to the ceiling: coils of rope, lamps and lamp-oil, candles in bundles, sacks of meal; everything a traveller forgets, and the smell of tallow over it all. Euphemia, a chandler, is here.

pages.label: go(region__edge_east_road,region__edge_east)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. For an hour the road runs under trees, and the light comes down green and broken through the leaves. It is a long walk, and your feet are sore by the end. The road ends where the land of Faennmeós does, on shingle above the tide-line, and beyond it is the Eastern Ocean, grey and moving as far as can be seen. No road goes on from here; what lies over the water is reached by ship, if at all.

pages.label: go(region__tl_edge_east,region__t19)
pages.page: Wet ground, sedge and cotton-grass, the pools reflecting the sky, a heron getting up slow and offended. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw18_19,region__t18)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. An axe is going in the wood, a long way off, and you never see the woodman. Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw18_38,region__t38)
pages.page: Water stands on both sides, and the path between is soft enough to take the print of your boot and keep it. Reed-beds whispering in the wind, and a bittern in them booming like a blown jar. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw17_36,region__t36)
pages.page: Old coppice gone wild, each stool grown into a clump of stems as thick as a leg. To the north the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw35_36,region__t35)
pages.page: The shadows are long when you leave the woods of Ashurst, and getting longer. There are no trees up here, and after the first mile no walls: only the path, the sky, and the long backs of the hills. High ground, rock breaking through the turf, and below, when you turn, the whole country laid out small. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw34_55,region__t34)
pages.page: Up on the tops there is nothing but heather, sky and wind, and a cairn now and then to say you are still on the path. The light goes before you are halfway, and you walk the rest by guess and by the pale line of the path. High ground, rock breaking through the turf, and below, when you turn, the whole country laid out small.

pages.label: go(region__tw15_34,region__t15)
pages.page: You set out from the fells of Cloudfell. The path climbs onto open moor, and the country falls away behind you in long brown folds. A saddle between two tops, boggy, with the cloud sitting on both of them. To the west the land rises.

pages.label: region__survey(party,region__t15)
pages.page: You stand a while on the highest ground to hand and look out over the country, learning the lie of it: where the land rises and falls, where the water runs, what stands on it. To the south-east, some way off: Broadford. To the south, a long way off: a long range of roofs behind a gate-arch. To the south, a long way off: Sedgeminster.

pages.label: go(region__tw14_15,region__t14)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. The path goes up by stony steps and down by rougher ones, and it is windy on every rise. Grey crag above and scree below, with a raven croaking over.

pages.label: go(region__tw14_33,region__t33)
pages.page: Sheep stand on the path and move off only when you are close. High ground, rock breaking through the turf, and below, when you turn, the whole country laid out small.

pages.label: go(region__tw13_33,region__t13)
pages.page: Woodland: oak and ash and holly, the light green and broken, last year’s leaves deep underfoot. To the east the land rises. A shepherd with a crook and a young dog at heel, looking about as if for something lost, is here.

pages.label: go(region__tw13_32,region__t32)
pages.page: A beck coming down in falls between the rocks, loud, and cold to the hand. To the east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw12_32,region__t12)
pages.page: A stand of tall trees with little under them, so that you can see a long way between the trunks, and nothing moving. To the south the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw11_31,region__t31)
pages.page: Close wood, old and mossy, the paths between the trunks made by animals and going where animals go. To the east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tr47_s1_s2_way,region__t47)
pages.page: It is easy going through open country: a mill, a ford, a man ploughing who stops to watch you go by. Peat ground cut once into steps, and long since flooded. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight. To the south-west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw26_47,region__t26)
pages.page: Water stands on both sides, and the path between is soft enough to take the print of your boot and keep it. Fen: reeds taller than a man, black water between, and the ground giving underfoot with every step. To the north-east the land rises. A pedlar with a pack on a frame and a staff, walking the drove-ways between the farms, is here. A pedlar is coming the other way along the sheep-track, bent under a pack on a frame, and lifts his staff to you from a long way off.

pages.label: go(region__tw26_46,region__t46)
pages.page: Out on the fen the sky is enormous, and the only things standing up in all that flatness are you and a heron. Alder carr standing in its own black water, the roots like knuckles. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight. To the north-west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw46_66,region__t66)
pages.page: The path goes out across the fen on a raised bank, reed on either hand taller than a man, open water glinting through it. A causey of old turves across the marsh, and on either side of it water that does not show how deep it is.

pages.label: go(region__tw65_66,region__t65)
pages.page: For a while the path keeps company with a river, close enough to hear it. Open water and mud among willow stumps, smelling of rot and mint. The Swanwater runs through it, and has to be waded or gone round.

pages.label: go(region__tw65_86,region__t86)
pages.page: Fen: reeds taller than a man, black water between, and the ground giving underfoot with every step. To the north the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw86_87,region__t87)
pages.page: Reed-beds whispering in the wind, and a bittern in them booming like a blown jar. To the north-west the land rises. A curlew, a tall brown-streaked wader with long legs and a long down-curved bill, is here.

pages.label: go(region__tw87_88,region__t88)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. Night comes on while you are still on the path, and you walk the last of it in the dark. Reed-beds whispering in the wind, and a bittern in them booming like a blown jar. To the east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw68_69,region__t69)
pages.page: The path goes into the wood, and the wood closes over it, and for a long time there is nothing to see but the next bend. A stand of tall trees with little under them, so that you can see a long way between the trunks, and nothing moving. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight. To the east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw69_70,region__t70)
pages.page: For an hour the path runs under trees, and the light comes down green and broken through the leaves. Beech wood, grey trunks over a floor of copper leaves, and very little sound. To the south-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw70_71,region__t71)
pages.page: An axe is going in the wood, a long way off, and you never see the woodman. Close wood, old and mossy, the paths between the trunks made by animals and going where animals go. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw71_92,region__t92)
pages.page: You leave the woods of Ashurst with your hood up and the rain in your face. Larks go up out of the grass on either hand, and come down again behind you. Flat grazing on close, springy turf, and willows along a ditch you cannot see.

pages.label: go(region__tw92_112,region__t112)
pages.page: Close wood, old and mossy, the paths between the trunks made by animals and going where animals go. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight. To the north the land rises. Fairholt is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__tw112_132,region__t132)
pages.page: Birch and rowan on a slope, the light coming white through the leaves. To the north the land rises. Fairholt is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__tw111_132,region__t111)
pages.page: The path runs between hedges and small fields, past a farm or two where dogs bark at you over the gate. Grassland, rolling a little, cropped short by sheep you cannot see. A wall of fieldstone runs along nowhere in particular. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight. To the north-east the land rises. Merscstede is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__tr111_s2_s4_way,region__s2_s4_way)
pages.page: Woods close in on both sides of the road between Merscstede and Fairholt, and open again at clearings. Deer go off between the trees without a sound. A milestone leans in the grass at the roadside, half sunk: on its face a worn wheel, and over it, if you look closely, the points of a crown. A messenger is going hard toward Fairholt, half running, with a satchel held to her side: Andry, who does not stop. Yarrow grows in the grass at the wayside, flat white heads over feathery leaves: a soldier’s herb, for cuts. Feverwort grows along the road in the rough grass, bitter-leaved: the herb-wives dry it for a child’s fever. Amaranth grows along the road, its dark red tassels hanging over the beds. Asters grow along the road in clumps, mauve with yellow eyes. Bamboo grows along the road in a dense clump, its canes knocking together in the wind. Gilliflowers grow along the road, pink and white, smelling of cloves. Woodbine climbs along the road, its cream and yellow flowers sweet at dusk. Stellaria grows along the road, its white flowers split like stars. Purslane grows along the road, low, with small fleshy leaves. Sweetgrass grows along the road, its long blades smelling of hay. Groundbread grows along the road, broad-leaved, with small white flowers.

pages.label: go(region__s1_stones_way,region__s1_stones_top)
pages.page: The path comes out on the top of the hill among fallen stones. An arch stands on its own against the sky, and beyond it the broken wall of something long and high. Below, Misthythe is all roofs and smoke. From up here the country lies open. Far off to the east you can make out a broken keep.

pages.label: go(region__s1_stones_up,region__s1_stones_hall)
pages.page: A long hall with no roof. Steps go up at the far end to a dais, and on it stand figures cut from the stone, taller than men, their faces worn smooth. Grass grows between the floor-slabs. Letters are cut along the edge of the dais, deep and square, in no hand anyone in Misthythe could read.

pages.label: go(region__s1_stones_arch,region__s1_stones_dome)
pages.page: A dome of stone as wide as a church, open to the sky in its crown, so that a round of light moves slowly over the floor through the day. Round the walls are low slabs, each with a hollow in it the length of a body, and nothing in any of them. Two pale lights come off the empty slabs and go round you, slowly, at the height a man carries a candle. The air goes cold. Lights in the dome will give you 7 minutes, no more.

pages.label: go(region__s1_stones_up,region__s1_stones_hall)
pages.page: A long hall with no roof. Letters are cut along the edge of the dais, deep and square, in no hand anyone in Misthythe could read.

pages.label: go(region__s1_stones_round,region__s1_stones_tree)
pages.page: A tree older than the stones, its trunk wider than a cart is long, its roots heaving up the turf. Strips of cloth are tied to its lowest branches, old and new: the folk of Misthythe still come up here. There is room on the low branches for another strip of cloth.

pages.label: go(region__s1_waterside_way,region__s1_green)
pages.page: Boats lie drawn up keel to keel on the shingle at Misthythe, and the houses come right down to them, nets hung on every fence. Magot is crying wares along the street: pots mended, knives ground. Hild is darning the hem of a red stage cloak. Isot the bookkeeper is weighing a handful of nails on a small brass scale. Averil the conspirator is shuffling a worn pack of cards one-handed. The inn’s dog lies across the doorstep of the Laughing Flame with his chin on his paws, and watches who comes. A thin brown cat crouches at the foot of a wall, watching a hole in it without a blink. A notice is nailed to the post by the well, written over in several hands. A strip of vellum is nailed to the post by the well, in a fair clerk’s hand, with a lead seal pressed in a blob of wax. A tall wagon, painted with a sun and a moon and the words GOSSE’S COMPANY in red letters gone pink, stands on the landing at Misthythe with its shafts down. A chain runs from its back wheel to a post, and the chain has a padlock on it. Wapshott’s bill on the wall says NOW PLAYING, NIGHTLY AT SEVEN, ADMISSION ONE COIN, CHILDREN AND DOGS HALF, on a strip pasted over the word COMING. The spring-head by the green has been running low for a year. The rope comes up with a hand’s depth of brown water in the bucket and a smell of wet stone, and the women who draw it do so in silence, to save breath. Aldous Fenn, the reeve of the wood-wardens, who license the cutting in the woods round Misthythe, is here. Hesper Lowe, a boat-wright’s apprentice with a drawing of a bell, is here. The old woman in the doorway, the innkeeper’s mother, who has not been out of her chair since the harvest and who asks, every morning, whether the lamp has been lit, is here. So are Absalom Gosse, Hepzibah Dimmock and Jem Pudding.

pages.label: go(region__s1_waterside_way,region__s1_waterside)
pages.page: Boats are drawn up on the bank, nets dry on poles, and a plank jetty runs out over the water. The water slaps against its piles, and the mud smells of weed. Odile has a net spread over three fences and is walking along it, looking for holes.

pages.label: talk_to(region__s1_r2)
pages.page: ‘Let me guess,’ says Odile. ‘You want something.’

pages.label: go(region__gate_ghessil_road,region__gate_ghessil)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. The road runs along a river for a mile, with alders on the bank and the water loud over the stones. The last mile is slow going. The road goes on into the Ghessil Uplands. Ahead, a light lying on the uplands that does not move when the clouds do.

pages.label: go(region__tw123_142,region__t123)
pages.page: It is easy going through open country: a mill, a ford, a man ploughing who stops to watch you go by. Meadow, wet in the hollows and dry on the rises, with a few thorn trees leaning all the same way.

pages.label: region__survey(party,region__t123)
pages.page: You stand a while on the highest ground to hand and look out over the country, learning the lie of it: where the land rises and falls, where the water runs, what stands on it. To the north-west, not far off: a walled keep on its rise. To the north, not far off: the fallen walls. To the south-east, some way off: the alder island.

pages.label: go(region__gate_corrow_road,region__gate_corrow)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. For a while the road keeps company with a river, close enough to hear it. The road goes on into the Corrow. Ahead, a mountain hanging in the sky, with nothing under it but air.

pages.label: go(region__tl_gate_corrow,region__t22)
pages.page: Woodland: oak and ash and holly, the light green and broken, last year’s leaves deep underfoot. Misthythe is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__tw21_22,region__t21)
pages.page: The path goes into the wood, and the wood closes over it, and for a long time there is nothing to see but the next bend. A stand of tall trees with little under them, so that you can see a long way between the trunks, and nothing moving.

pages.label: go(region__tw21_41,region__t41)
pages.page: For an hour the path runs under trees, and the light comes down green and broken through the leaves. Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed. A moth, a large moth with soft grey-brown wings marked with eyes, its feathered feelers spread, is here.

pages.label: wait_for_dark
pages.page: A pedlar is coming the other way along the sheep-track, bent under a pack on a frame, and lifts his staff to you from a long way off.

pages.label: go(region__tw40_41,region__t40)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. An axe is going in the wood, a long way off, and you never see the woodman. Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed.

pages.label: go(region__tw80_81,region__t81)
pages.page: Beech wood, grey trunks over a floor of copper leaves, and very little sound. To the north-west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw81_101,region__t101)
pages.page: The shadows are long when you leave the woods of Asholt, and getting longer. Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed.

pages.label: go(region__tw101_122,region__t122)
pages.page: It is easy going through open country: a mill, a ford, a man ploughing who stops to watch you go by. Long grass gone to seed, and the wind combing it one way and then the other.

pages.label: go(region__tw123_142,region__t142)
pages.page: Out on the fen the sky is enormous, and the only things standing up in all that flatness are you and a heron. The light goes before you are halfway, and you walk the rest by guess and by the pale line of the path. Wet ground, sedge and cotton-grass, the pools reflecting the sky, a heron getting up slow and offended. To the north the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw141_142,region__t141)
pages.page: You set out from the fen of Duskmoss. The path goes out across the fen on a raised bank, reed on either hand taller than a man, open water glinting through it. Alder carr standing in its own black water, the roots like knuckles. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw121_141,region__t121)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. Pine wood, the ground soft with needles and the smell of resin heavy in the still air. To the east the land rises. A hedgehog, a small brown hedgehog with a coat of pale-tipped spines and a pointed, whiskered snout, is here.

pages.label: talk_to(region__s1_apothecary_keeper)
pages.page: ‘A stranger!’ says Leofric, pleased. ‘Sit, if you like. Ask, if you like.’

pages.label: take_leave(region__s1_apothecary_keeper)
pages.page: ‘Come back and tell me how it goes!’ calls Leofric after you.

pages.label: go(region__edge_north_road,region__edge_north)
pages.page: You walk fast to keep warm, and it does not help much. For a while the road keeps company with a river, close enough to hear it. A wayside cross of the brothers of Reodweard stands where the road leaves Faennmeós, a cross cut in a pillar of old stone with the makers’ marks still under it, and a dish at its foot for offerings. Beyond it the road goes on north into Blóstmawudu, forest country, the folk say. Few of them have been.

pages.label: go(region__tw25_26,region__t25)
pages.page: Beech wood, grey trunks over a floor of copper leaves, and very little sound.

pages.label: go(region__tw4_24,region__t24)
pages.page: For an hour the path runs under trees, and the light comes down green and broken through the leaves. Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed. Misthythe is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__tw24_45,region__t45)
pages.page: An axe is going in the wood, a long way off, and you never see the woodman. Pine wood, the ground soft with needles and the smell of resin heavy in the still air. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight.

pages.label: talk_to(region__wr44)
pages.page: A pedlar grins before you have said anything at all. ‘You look like a person with a question.’

pages.label: go(region__tw25_45,region__t25)
pages.page: It is cold enough to see your breath, and the ruts are hard with frost. The path goes into the wood, and the wood closes over it, and for a long time there is nothing to see but the next bend. Beech wood, grey trunks over a floor of copper leaves, and very little sound.

pages.label: go(region__tw5_6,region__t6)
pages.page: Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed. To the east the land rises. A stack of cordwood under turf smokes in the clearing, and on one side the turf has slipped and flame shows through it. The charcoal-burner, a collier black to the elbows, minding a smoking stack in a clearing, is here.

pages.label: go(region__tw7_26,region__t26)
pages.page: You set out from the woods of Ashurst. Water stands on both sides, and the path between is soft enough to take the print of your boot and keep it. Fen: reeds taller than a man, black water between, and the ground giving underfoot with every step. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw25_46,region__t46)
pages.page: The path goes out across the fen on a raised bank, reed on either hand taller than a man, open water glinting through it. Alder carr standing in its own black water, the roots like knuckles. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight. To the north-west the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tr46_s1_s2_way,region__s1_s2_way)
pages.page: The path runs along a river for a mile, with alders on the bank and the water loud over the stones. The road between Misthythe and Merscstede goes through scattered woods and the clearings of charcoal-burners. A stag stands in a clearing, watching, before it turns away. By the road stands an old milestone, worn to a stub, with a wheel cut in it and something over the wheel that might once have been a crown. The road is churned by cattle, all going toward Misthythe, and not long since: some of it is still warm. Willows lean out over the water along the road, grey-green, their roots in the bank and their long shoots trailing in the current. Sphagnum moss lies in the wet hollows, red and green, holding water like a sponge: it binds a wound better than linen. Comfrey grows rank by the water, hairy-leaved, its bells hanging: knitbone, the herb-wives call it. Dragonwort grows along the road, a red spike among spearing leaves. Bloodroot grows along the road, broad-leaved, with white flowers low to the ground. Celandine grows along the road, yellow-starred in the damp. Cinquefoil runs over the ground along the road, its small yellow flowers five-petalled. Daffodils grow along the road in a bank, their strap-leaves in clumps. Alhuren grows along the road, silver-leaved, its blue flowers pale as a candle-flame. Rosenoble grows along the road, a briar of deep red roses. Hazel grows along the road, broad-leaved, its nuts in clusters of three. Hyssop grows along the road in spikes of blue, bees working it. Staggerweed grows along the road, tall, with spurred blue flowers. Pennyroyal grows along the road, low and minty, with small purple flowers. Poppies grow along the road, red among the beds. Thistles grow along the road, purple-headed. Tansy grows along the road, its yellow buttons over feathery leaves. A dropberry bush grows along the road, its red berries hanging in strings. Starwort grows along the road, small and white-flowered. Actaea grows along the road, its white flowers in feathery spikes. Bruisewort grows along the road, thick-leaved, with small purple flowers. Betony stands in the short grass at the wood’s edge, purple-spiked: the hedge herb, for a cut or a sting.

pages.label: go(region__s1_waterside_way,region__s1_waterside)
pages.page: Boats are drawn up on the bank, nets dry on poles, and a plank jetty runs out over the water. The water slaps against its piles, and the mud smells of weed. Robin is knotting a net with a wooden needle. You take Bran’s tally-stick.

pages.label: go(region__s1_waterside_way,region__s1_green)
pages.page: A quay of grey stone runs out into the water at Porthalen, its edge worn round and green with weed, and the town climbs behind it. Gulls sit along it in a row, facing the wind, over the slap of water on stone. The Whitewater runs by below the houses. Twice this month the Hall’s keeper has driven the town’s pigs off the verge of the old road. The geese are kept in a bunch at the well, hissing at the lane to the Hall, and three hens have gone from the inn’s yard since Tuesday. Across the green the customs-house door stands open, and a customs-man in the Rì’s blue leans on the jamb with his staff. From the pens beyond comes the bawling of cattle nobody has fed. Over the salt-houses only one chimney is smoking, thin and grey. A salter stands in a doorway looking up the river with his arms folded. A boat is coming in under half its sail, and a man waits on the quay with a coil of rope over his arm. A notice is nailed to the post by the well, newer than the others, the reeve’s seal at its foot. On the landing a man is caulking the seams of a flat-bottomed boat no longer than a cart, and three more stand finished on trestles with a chalked price on each: thirty. Sabine is crying wares along the street: pots mended, knives ground. Thurstan is showing a boy how to hold a staff, and correcting his feet without a word. Aldred stands by the door with a cudgel at his belt, watching the street. Baldric the painting master is weighing a handful of nails on a small brass scale. The inn’s dog lies across the doorstep of the Stone Horn with his chin on his paws, and watches who comes. Owain stands at the edge of the quay with his hands in his armpits, watching the customs-house door. A woman in black sits on the step of a cold house with her hands in her lap, watching the road. Dandelions stand in the grass, yellow and seeding: a tea of them cleans the blood. A bay tree grows in the gardens about the green, dark and glossy, clipped for its leaves. A notice is nailed to the post by the well, written over in several hands. A strip of vellum is nailed to the post by the well, in a fair clerk’s hand, with a lead seal pressed in a blob of wax. A notice in a clerk’s hand is nailed to the post by the well: THE SEA-GATE AT GATESEND IS TO BE MENDED BEFORE THE SPRING TIDE. THIRTY CROWNS OF THE REEVE TO WHOEVER MENDS IT. A. TALFRYN, REEVE. The spring-head by the green has been running low for a year. The rope comes up with a hand’s depth of brown water in the bucket and a smell of wet stone, and the women who draw it do so in silence, to save breath. The factor, who keeps the books of the Guldríce company, is here. Aldous Fenn, the reeve of the wood-wardens, who license the cutting in the woods round Porthalen, is here. Hesper Lowe, a boat-wright’s apprentice with a drawing of a bell, is here. So are the surveyor’s son, Reeve Annis Talfryn, Gwil Pryce and the woman in black. Patch thumps his tail on the ground without getting up.

pages.label: go(region__edge_east_road,region__edge_east)
pages.page: Showers come over one after another, and between them the sun comes out on the wet country. The road goes into the wood, and the wood closes over it, and for a long time there is nothing to see but the next bend. The road runs out among dunes and marram grass, and past them is the Eastern Ocean: a line of surf, and the open water beyond it to the edge of the sky. Whatever is out there is a voyage away, not a walk.

pages.label: go(region__tl_edge_east,region__t258)
pages.page: Bramble and hazel thick under the trees, and a way through only where the deer have pushed. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight.

pages.label: go(region__tw237_258,region__t237)
pages.page: For an hour the path runs under trees, and the light comes down green and broken through the leaves. Birch and rowan on a slope, the light coming white through the leaves. A road crosses it, the only straight thing in sight. Porthalen is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__tw236_256,region__t256)
pages.page: It rains on and off the whole way, a fine rain that soaks through your clothes. Old coppice gone wild, each stool grown into a clump of stems as thick as a leg.

pages.label: go(region__tw256_275,region__t275)
pages.page: The path runs along a river for a mile, with alders on the bank and the water loud over the stones. Alder carr standing in its own black water, the roots like knuckles. The Whitewater runs through it, and has to be waded or gone round. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw275_276,region__t276)
pages.page: For a while the path keeps company with a river, close enough to hear it. Alder carr standing in its own black water, the roots like knuckles. The Whitewater runs through it, and has to be waded or gone round. To the north-east the land rises.

pages.label: go(region__tw276_277,region__t277)
pages.page: Alder carr standing in its own black water, the roots like knuckles. The Whitewater runs through it, and has to be waded or gone round. To the north the land rises. Porthalen is close by: you can hear it, and smell its smoke.

pages.label: go(region__edge_south_road,region__s1_green)
pages.page: You leave the march-stone of Cloudwold late, in rain, with the light going early under the cloud. Porthalen shows ahead a long while before you reach it: smoke, a roofline, the noise of it on the wind. A quay of grey stone runs out into the water at Porthalen, its edge worn round and green with weed, and the town climbs behind it. The inn’s dog lies across the doorstep of the Stone Horn with his chin on his paws, and watches who comes. Owain stands at the edge of the quay with his hands in his armpits, watching the customs-house door. A woman in black sits on the step of a cold house with her hands in her lap, watching the road. Hesper Lowe, a boat-wright’s apprentice with a drawing of a bell, is here. So are Reeve Annis Talfryn, Gwil Pryce and the woman in black. The bailiff’s men have been through again. The price is five crowns a hearth now, and the reeve has been seen reading the receipt by the well and putting it in his pocket. The surveyor’s son has gone: his mule is not at the rail, and the boy at the stable says he was gone before light, with a spade. The merchant keeps looking up the road with the face of a person doing sums.

Up on the hill above the roofs, in the dome of the old stones, a pale light goes round and round.

pages.label: go(region__s1_drill_gate,region__s1_drill)
pages.page: A square of beaten earth behind the Stone Horn, a rack of blunted blades along one wall and a post hacked pale at the height of a man’s neck. Whoever teaches here will show a technique to anyone who has done enough to be worth the showing, and can pay for it. Odile teaches Cleave, Feint and Taunt, 35 coin a lesson: an hour’s work, and only to one who has done enough out in the world to have earned it. On the rack by the gate, for sale and not for practice, are a fine handaxe, a fine longbow and a fine greatsword. Odile, a master-at-arms, who teaches for 35 coin a lesson, is here.

pages.label: talk_to(region__s1_drill_master)
pages.page: Odile looks up, and puts her hands still, and waits for you to say what you want.

pages.label: take_leave(region__s1_drill_master)
pages.page: Odile lifts a hand, once.

pages.label: go(region__s1_stones_way,region__s1_stones_top)
pages.page: The path comes out on the top of the hill among fallen stones. An arch stands on its own against the sky, and beyond it the broken wall of something long and high. Below, Porthalen is all roofs and smoke. From up here the country lies open. Far off to the north you can make out a broken keep.

pages.label: go(pans__boiling_door,pans__boiling)
pages.page: Three iron pans the size of a cart-floor stand over brick hearths, the brine in them grey and still. Only one hearth is lit, low, fed with broken barrel-staves. A crust of salt is setting on the cold ones like ice.

pages.label: go(pans__boiling_door,region__s1_shop)
pages.page: Salt in sacks stacked to the rafters, barrels of fish in brine along the wall, and a smell of tar and the sea that gets into everything. Holgar, a salter, is here.

pages.label: go(region__s1_herbs_door,region__s1_herbs)
pages.page: Bunches of drying herbs hang from every beam, so that you walk in stooping, and the air is thick with sage, mint and wormwood. Wulfrun, a herbalist, is here.

pages.label: go(region__s1_sheds_way,region__s1_green)
pages.page: A quay of grey stone runs out into the water at Porthalen, its edge worn round and green with weed, and the town climbs behind it. Rain is falling, and people keep to their doorways. pages.label: go(region__s1_fields_way,region__s1_fields)
pages.page: Strips of field run out from the houses to the hedges, with a trodden track between them. Rooks rise and settle behind whoever is working, and the turned earth smells raw. Dunstan is cleaning a long narrow spade, the turf-iron, with a handful of grass. Martin is leaning on a gate, looking at a field of beans gone black with fly.
